brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Strong organism metaphor with glowing nucleus and orbiting particles makes abstract metrics feel alive and emotionally legible
Restrained dark palette with red/green dichotomy reads instantly as stress vs. calm without explicit labeling
Clean typographic hierarchy and generous negative space let the two organisms breathe as the focal subject
dominant_weaknesses: Static screenshot cannot convey the breathing/pulsing behavior that is the entire premise — motion is the product
Hard vertical divider plus mirrored layouts feel like two dashboard cards, undermining the singular ecosystem fiction
Data chrome (Processes, Threads, Load Average) is generic monitor-speak that contradicts the organic vocabulary above
fix_priorities: Demonstrate motion: show pulse cadence, particle orbit speed, membrane wobble tied to load thresholds
Dissolve the divider — let organisms share one habitat so they can interact (e.g., CPU stress radiates toward memory)
Rewrite footer/legend metrics in the organism register (heartbeat, metabolism) to keep metaphor coherent
Add subtle stress cues: jittered particles, asymmetric glow, or tighter orbits at 92% to make the red truly feel distressed
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective land well via the metaphor, but behavioral falls short because the static frame hides the motion that would make state legible at a glance.
rationale.intent_fit: Conceptually nails the organism framing and color-codes stress vs. health, but without visible motion behavior the brief is only half-delivered.
